source: Minchat Shai on Gen 10:19 (Ramah's four-member qere list)
claim_en: וצבים ("and Tzevoyim," the border-list) — WRITTEN doubly defective, no vav and one yod, READ וצבוים (the Ramah's rule for this token; the Yerushalmi's two-yod spelling recorded and rejected). SNAPSHOT: the bare written skeleton locked. Instrument note: here the written/read pair is SINGLE-token encoded (the read-form living in the pronunciation layer), where 8:17's pair was dual-token — the encoding varies by site.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 10:2 (Ramah — the Tubal rule's own anchor)
claim_en: ותבל ("and Tubal," Japheth's son) — defective in all books (the Yerushalmi's ותובל rejected): the same Ramah note gen_13 verified from the other side — plene תובל belongs to Tubal-Cain's two tokens alone; Japheth's son goes bare. The rule now locked at BOTH its anchors.

כנמרד גבור ציד ("like Nimrod, a MIGHTY hunter" — the proverb) — "this one alone plene with vav in the Torah in this phrasing; the first of this verse and all the rest defective": SNAPSHOT agrees to the letter — the narrative's mighty-words (10:8, and the verse's own first) bare, the PROVERB'S plene: the saying carries the full spelling.
כנמרד ("like Nimrod") — "without maqqef" (the joining hyphen): the name stands free in the proverb. SNAPSHOT's maqqef column agrees.
רחבת עיר ("Rehovot-City," Asshur's build-list) — doubly defective in the precise majority, "and the Masorah on it: unique-defective." SNAPSHOT letter-exact.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 10:31 (all books + Ramah vs Hilleli; Onkelos vs Yonatan)
claim_en: לגויהם ("BY their nations," Shem's closing formula) — with LAMED in all our books and the Ramah; the Hilleli reads בגויהם with bet — and the TRANSLATIONS split as witnesses: Onkelos rendered like the bet, Yonatan ben Uzziel precisely like the lamed. SNAPSHOT: lamed — and the neighboring verse's בגויהם (10:32, bet) locked beside it by the Ramah's complementary rule.

על כן יאמר ("therefore it is SAID") — the Kitzur's trio: Nimrod's proverb (10:9), "therefore it is said in the Book of the Wars of the LORD" (Num 21:14), and "of Zion it shall be said" (Ps 87:5) — the war-hero, the war-book, and the city where every native is mighty. Torah-side: the passive said-word's only two tokens; the Psalms leg is an inheritance edge.
חצרמות ("Hazarmavet") — the Ramah: ONE WORD, the resh with sheva (Chronicles' parallel list spells its own way — see the edge layer). SNAPSHOT: a single token, letters locked.

עובל ("Obal") — plene with vav HERE; "and in Chronicles with a yod" (עיבל, I Chr 1:22): the same man spelled differently across the two lists — a cross-book variant the tradition itself indexes. SNAPSHOT: the Torah spelling locked.
נפרדו הגוים ("the nations DIVIDED") — the gimel with dagesh (doubling dot). SNAPSHOT agrees.

"The printer ERRED making a paragraph break here" (before Ham's line) — though the Hilleli HAS a section here, "all Torah scrolls of Jerusalem and Ashkenaz have none, and neither Rambam nor Meiri" count one: a PARAGRAPH DISPUTE between the codices themselves. SNAPSHOT carries no paragraph instrumentation — gap class of G12-11, now with a documented two-camp case.

check.note: petucha/setuma uninstrumented; this site is a genuine inter-codex paragraph dispute (Hilleli yes; Jerusalem/Ashkenaz scrolls, Rambam, Meiri no)

claim_en: THE ROSTER IS RESOLVED TO REAL PLACES, AND THE SEATS DISAGREE WITH ONE ANOTHER. Each name in our chapter is identified with a contemporary nation or city, and the two great identification lists do NOT align: one aligns Gomer with Germania and Madai with Macedonia, the other gives Magog as Kandiya and Madai as Macedonia on a different reckoning, with Tiras disputed between Persia and Thrace and ruled for Persia at one seat. The city names of 10:10-12 are likewise resolved twice over. The variance is recorded rather than harmonised: this unit's register maps to the world through two competing gazetteers.

check.note: A genealogical register resolved to real geography by two seats whose identifications conflict; both gazetteers carried.

claim_en: A COMPARATIVE PARTICLE TURNS A NAME INTO A TYPE. Our 10:9 does not say people would speak OF Nimrod but that they would say 'כְּנִמְרֹד (ke-Nimrod, LIKE Nimrod), a mighty hunter before the Lord' - the comparative verified in the ink at derivation. From that particle the chain reads the verse as establishing a TYPE rather than reporting a reputation, and later figures are measured against it: Esau hunts with his mouth as this one ensnared with words. The same clause enters a census of five ill-omened uses of the word 'he'.

check.note: A comparative particle in the ink read as converting a proper name into a reusable type; the particle verified present at derivation.

claim_en: THIS UNIT'S BIRTH ORDER IS USED AS AN ARITHMETIC PREMISE TO DECIDE A DIFFERENT VERSE'S MEANING. Because our 10:6 lists Mizraim before Canaan, Mizraim is the elder - and therefore the statement that Hebron was built seven years before Zoan cannot mean founded, since no father builds for his younger son first. The word is accordingly parsed as meaning seven times more developed. A genealogical ordering in this unit constrains the parse of a verse in another book.

check.note: A listing order used as a premise in an argument that fixes the meaning of a word elsewhere in the corpus.

claim_en: OUR 10:19 IS THE HALAKHIC SOURCE OF A BORDER. The territorial extent named in a later book is resolved by citing this verse - 'the land of the Canaanite, to the Canaanite border, as it is said: the Canaanite border was from Sidon' - so a boundary in law is fixed by this unit's own geography operator. Set against it, the register of nations promised is counted at TEN where seven were given, and the three unidentified names are disputed across four different identification sets.

check.note: A geography operator serving as the stated source of a legal boundary, with a promised-versus-given count dispute beside it.

claim_en: THIS UNIT'S GENERATIONS BECOME NAMED PRECEDENTS IN A STANDING CURSE FORMULA AND IN AN END-OF-DAYS CENSUS. The court's formula against one who reneges on a sale names them: 'He who exacted payment from the generation of the flood AND FROM THE GENERATION OF THE DISPERSION will exact payment from whoever does not stand by his word' - the two generations serving as the heavenly court's standing precedents. And the surviving 'third' of a prophetic census is computed off this genealogy's own nodes, disputed as a third of Shem's line or of the whole world's.

check.note: Two generations from this span used as named precedents in a live legal formula, and its nodes used as census denominators.
